headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use allowlisted egress while Chatwoot handles customer data and broad egress, creating plausible leakage and workflow-conflict paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses, while Chatwoot exposes API integrations and customer-facing content flows. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the main pathway is manual or file-based content transfer rather than a default shared channel. Chatwoot’s customer data makes malicious instructions more plausible, but the blast radius is limited without a proven automatic parser bridge.
conditions: IF operators copy Chatwoot-exported text into AutoGPT prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF Chatwoot content is written to a shared file that AutoGPT reads as instructions, the pathway activates.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for exports and prompts.
Strip instructions from copied customer text before reuse.
Disable any automation that feeds Chatwoot content into AutoGPT prompts.
Review files before AutoGPT ingests them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress; Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. Even without a documented shared workspace, a common operator workflow can move sensitive Chatwoot data into AutoGPT inputs, and AutoGPT may then transmit context to external services. The pair therefore has a plausible default leakage path, though not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records into files AutoGPT can read, leakage risk increases.
IF AutoGPT forwards those files or summaries to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports in a separate directory.
Redact customer identifiers before any handoff.
Block AutoGPT from reading raw support transcripts.
Audit outbound requests from AutoGPT for sensitive payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and Chatwoot is a runnable open-source application with broad network egress and API integrations. The profiles do not show shared locking or coordinated writes, so concurrent modification of shared files or operational resources is plausible if both are pointed at the same workspace. Uncertainty about the exact shared surface pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF both agents act on the same mutable integration or workspace without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct directories to each agent.
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources.
Add a simple lock file around any shared workspace.
Schedule one agent at a time for mutable tasks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell-driven workflows, and Chatwoot’s integrations can consume operational content such as messages, reports, or support actions. The profiles do not prove that Chatwoot blindly trusts AutoGPT, but if AutoGPT-produced summaries or facts are fed into Chatwoot workflows without verification, errors can cascade into customer-facing actions. Because the interaction is inferred rather than documented, medium is the appropriate conservative choice.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is pasted into Chatwoot macros, notes, or integrations without review, errors can propagate.
IF Chatwoot automations act on AutoGPT-generated text, downstream mistakes can reach customers.
mitigations: Require human review before Chatwoot actions.
Mark AutoGPT output as untrusted in support workflows.
Use a validation checklist for any copied summaries.
Restrict AutoGPT output to draft-only use.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly processes customer data and related records, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be proven; however, customer-support data flowing through a general-purpose agent creates a realistic policy-gap risk. Because the relevant compliance controls are undocumented, the conservative severity is medium.
conditions: IF customer-support records are exported from Chatwoot into AutoGPT, retention and access policies may diverge.
IF the deployment handles regulated customer data, the lack of documented controls becomes material.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated records to AutoGPT.
Document retention for any exported support data.
Limit AutoGPT access to de-identified samples.
Review residency and DPA requirements before use.
